metadata.title: Survey of Adult Skills 2023 Technical Report (EN)
metadata.venue: OECD Survey of Adult Skills 2023 Technical Report

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The document describes PIAAC Cycle 2 survey weighting and variance estimation procedures, including the computation of final person weights for adults aged 16–65 with completed background questionnaire (BQ) and literacy-related non-respondents (LRNRs) with completed doorstep interviews. Weighting incorporates selection probabilities, non-response adjustments (including separate treatment for literacy-related non-response), trimming of extreme weights, and calibration/benchmarking to population control totals (at minimum age and gender). Variance estimation is implemented via replicate weights using delete-one jackknife (JK1), paired jackknife (JK2), and balanced repeated replication (BRR) with Fay’s method; BRR with Fay’s adjustment is the recommended approach for most countries. The chapter does not provide a single ML analysis sample; therefore, weight application is described as part of the survey design for subsequent analyses rather than as a specific model-fitting step in this text.

confounders_identified: Education (highest education level; education by gender; education by age)
Ethnicity / mother tongue / language spoken at home
ISCO at 1-digit level (coded from open-ended parental occupation)
Work history (years of work experience; employer changes; career breaks; unemployment duration)
Job characteristics (working hours, earnings, job security, occupational status, match between education and work)
Social and emotional skills (Big Five: Open-Mindedness, Conscientiousness, Agreeableness, Extraversion, Emotional Stability; BFI-2-S / BFI-2-XS)
Work environment indicators (teamwork, knowledge sharing, social support, participation)
Work intensity / standardisation / short repetitive tasks
ICT use at work and in everyday life
Earnings reporting categories (open numeric questions; top-coding)
Doorstep interview variables (gender, age group, years of education broad categories, subjective status, born in country, time lived in country)
data.outcome_summary: This technical report chapter set does not train or evaluate machine-learning predictive models; instead, it documents (i) development and validation of the PIAAC Cycle 2 background questionnaire (BQ) and its translation/adaptation procedures, and (ii) survey weighting and variance estimation methods for PIAAC. For the BQ field trial (FT) validation, the report states that analyses used PIAAC Cycle 2 FT data collected in 2021, with a pooled cross-national FT sample of N=32,532 interviews in most analyses; item non-response was generally very low (often ≤1%), with higher non-response for open earnings questions and some occupation/industry items. Timing analyses show the international average core FT BQ duration for employed respondents was below the 45-minute target (e.g., 40:07 minutes for employed; 38:28 minutes excluding HRV), supporting no timing-driven shortening for the main study. For variance estimation, the report specifies replicate-weight approaches (JK1, JK2, BRR, BRR with Fay’s method) and recommends BRR with Fay’s adjustment (with perturbation factor 30%) for most countries, with France using JK2 due to its balanced design. No ML performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/RMSE) are reported because the focus is instrument and survey methodology rather than predictive modeling.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a technical report describing survey instrument development/validation and survey weighting/variance estimation for PIAAC Cycle 2, not an empirical ML study with predictive modeling outcomes. Therefore, no ML algorithms are evaluated (ml_techniques.all_techniques is empty) and no ML primary model can be identified. The only quantitative results provided relate to questionnaire timing, item non-response, and the weighting/replication framework rather than ML model performance.
